blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Video generation models have achieved remarkable visual fidelity and have strong potential to become general-purpose world simulators. Despite this progress, they still fail to generate videos which adhere to laws of physics. The problem becomes even more apparent in realistic settings where multiple physical principles must work together within the same video; for example, ‘a balloon floating upward while steam rises from a pot’ requires buoyancy and fluid dynamics to unfold coherently and simultaneously. Yet existing methods largely ignore multi-principle interactions, focusing on a single principle per video. We propose HiPhy ( Hi erarchical Phy sical Alignment), a reinforcement learning framework that grounds video generation in physical laws through a dual-level objective: locally enforcing the temporal dynamics of individual physical principles, and globally ensuring the physical and semantic coherence of the entire scene. To support multi-principle generation, we construct a 50K-prompt dataset and introduce a prompt benchmark MultiPhyBench , spanning a diverse range of co-occurring physical events. Our experiments show that HiPhy significantly outperforms prior methods and baselines, improving physical commonsense and semantic alignment significantly across various benchmarks, with the largest gains on scenes involving multiple concurrent physical principles where competing methods degrade most sharply.
blocks.zh: 视频生成模型实现了显著的视觉忠实,并具有成为通用世界模拟器的强大潜力. 尽管取得了这些进展,他们仍然未能产生遵守物理定律的视频。 这个问题在现实环境中变得更加明显,因为多种物理原理必须在同一个视频中一起工作;例如, " 气球在蒸汽从锅中升起时向上飘起 " ,需要浮力和流体动力,以连贯和同步地展开。 然而,现有的方法在很大程度上忽略了多原则的相互作用,侧重于每个视频的单一原则. 我们提出HiPhy(Hi erarchical Phy sy scial Unit),这是一个强化的学习框架,通过一个双重层面的目标将视频生成作为实体法的基础:局部执行单个物理原理的时间动态,全球确保整个场景的物理和语义一致性. 为了支持多原理生成,我们构建了一个50K-即时数据集,并引入了快速基准多Phy Bench,涵盖多种共同发生的物理事件. 我们的实验表明,HiPhy明显超越了先前的方法和基线,在各种基准之间大大地改进了物理常识和语义的相通性,在涉及多种同时存在的物理原理的场景上,竞争方法的下降幅度最大。

blocks.en: Video diffusion models [ 23 , 35 ] have made remarkable progress in producing high-resolution, temporally coherent videos [ 38 , 49 ] . This rapid progress has made video generation models promising candidates for general-purpose world simulators that are capable of synthesizing diverse physical scenarios on demand for embodied AI, robotics simulation, scientific visualization, and counterfactual reasoning [ 17 , 22 , 19 , 1 ] .
blocks.zh: 视频传播模式[23,35]在制作高清晰度,时间一致性的视频[38,49]方面取得了显著进展. 这一迅速的进展使视频生成模型对通用世界模拟器的候选者有希望,这些模拟器能够根据对体现的AI、机器人模拟、科学可视化和反事实推理的需求合成各种物理情景[17、22、19、1]。

blocks.en: Despite their visual fidelity, current video generators routinely produce clips that violate elementary physical laws, such as momentum, fluid dynamics, and material properties [ 22 , 17 ] . We argue this reflects a deeper representational gap: because models are trained merely to maximize frame likelihood given text [ 13 , 12 ] , they reproduce plausible patterns from their vast training data without reasoning about the underlying mechanisms [ 30 , 8 ] . Consider a prompt “an apple falls into water,” which entails two co-occurring physical principles: rigid-body and fluid dynamics (see Fig. 2 ). We find this representational gap manifests in two consistent failure modes on such compound prompts: (1) Principle Omission , where models ignore secondary physics, for instance, the apple drops realistically but the water remains undisturbed; and (2) Temporal Shortcutting , where unfolding dynamics are collapsed into a single visual snapshot, such as rendering the splash as a static spraying effect instead of progressing through impact → \rightarrow crown formation . Importantly, these failures do not reflect a deficit in visual capability; given sufficiently detailed text, modern video models generate individual physical principles with striking fidelity. The core challenge is finding a systematic mechanism to elicit this latent knowledge along two dimensions: the presence of each principle and its temporal structure. This motivates HiPhy ’s dual-level design: per-principle supervision targets Principle Omission , while fine-grained sub-stage reward design addresses Temporal Shortcutting .
blocks.zh: 目前的视频发电机尽管具有视觉忠实性,但经常产生违反基本物理定律的片段,如动能、流体动态和物质特性[22、17]。 我们认为,这反映了一个更深层次的代表性差距:由于对模型进行培训只是为了最大限度地扩大文本[13、12]中的框架可能性,因此它们从广泛的培训数据中复制了可信的模式,而没有对基本机制进行推理[30、8]。 考虑迅速的“苹果倒入水中”,这涉及两个共同发生的物理原理:刚体和流体动力(见图2)。 我们发现这种代表性差距表现在两种一致的失败模式上: (1) 原则排除,例如,模型忽略了次级物理,苹果的下降是现实的,但水仍未被扰动;和(2) 短暂的切割,即正在发生的动态崩溃成单一的视觉快照,例如将喷出物变成静态喷洒效果,而不是通过撞击推进------------------------。 重要的是,这些失败并不反映视觉能力不足;由于文字足够详细,现代视频模型产生个人物理原理,具有惊人的忠诚性。 核心挑战是找到一种系统机制,从两个方面获得这种潜在的知识:每项原则的存在及其时间结构。 这激励了HiPhy的双层设计:每个原则监督目标原则排放,而精细分级奖励设计则涉及Temperal shortcution。

blocks.en: Existing efforts to inject physical knowledge into video models largely rely on 3D engines [ 27 , 29 , 6 ] , fine-tuning [ 5 , 41 , 11 , 40 ] , or inference-time guidance [ 48 , 14 , 45 , 25 , 33 , 16 ] . While 3D engines can simulate concurrent dynamics, they are computationally heavy and constrained to rigid domains. Conversely, learning-based and guidance methods offer flexibility but typically supervise only a single physical principle per video. Consequently, they lack mechanisms to ensure compound events are jointly satisfied. Empirically, we observe these latter methods degrade sharply as concurrent processes increase, often dropping one principle entirely.
blocks.zh: 现有将物理知识注入视频模型的努力主要依靠3D引擎[27,29,6],微调[5,41,11,40],或推论时间指导[48,14,45,25,33,16]. 虽然3D引擎可以模拟并发的动力学,但它们在计算上很重并受刚性域所制约. 相反,基于学习和指导的方法提供了灵活性,但通常只监督每个视频的单一物理原则。 因此,它们缺乏确保共同满足复合事件的机制。 从经验上讲,我们观察到后一种方法随着并行过程的增加而急剧退化,往往完全放弃了一种原则。

blocks.en: In this paper, we propose HiPhy ( Hi erarchical Phy sical Alignment), a reinforcement learning framework that closes the previously mentioned gap by formulating compound physical events as a hierarchical alignment problem. By optimizing each physical principle locally, HiPhy enables physically grounded video generation in concurrent, multi-principle scenes. Our key insight is that physical plausibility is fundamentally both a temporal and a compositional property. While modern video generators struggle to reason about the temporal progression of physical events, leading to Principle Omission and Temporal Shortcutting , we model multi-principle scenes as compositions of independent, temporally structured physical principles. Consequently, we introduce a novel training objective that explicitly enforces stage-level supervision across each concurrent physical principle. HiPhy mirrors this insight through a hierarchical alignment framework. At the foundational level, we explicitly optimize for the chronological progression of each physical event by breaking it into smaller stages. At the same time, we align these stages with global video coherence and semantic alignment objectives, ensuring that multi-principle interactions compose naturally while maintaining semantic and visual coherence. Crucially, when a prompt contains multiple concurrent physical events, HiPhy treats each as an independent learning stream, preventing high-variance signals from washing out the gradient. blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Physically Plausible Video Generation One line of work fine-tunes video backbones on large physically annotated datasets [ 5 , 41 , 11 , 40 ] . Because such models lack explicit physical knowledge, generation quality remains tightly coupled to training-set coverage and rarely transfers to the diversity of real-world scenarios [ 30 , 17 ] . A second line injects physical knowledge through 3D engines such as Blender or Unreal, depth or edge predictors, or auxiliary 3D objectives [ 27 , 29 , 21 ] , and graphics rendering pipelines [ 2 ] . These methods are precise but constrained to fixed physical categories and incur heavy computational cost, particularly for phenomena such as fluids or steam [ 6 ] . Additionally, some works introduce auxiliary signals at inference time, including coarse intermediate representations [ 48 , 14 ] , off-the-shelf verifiers and judges [ 45 , 25 ] , and test-time optimization [ 33 , 16 ] . Verifier-based methods either require large memory budgets or incur long inference times, and test-time optimization typically refines trajectories without addressing implausible initial plans. While prior work holistically supervises a single physical principle per video, HiPhy is the first framework to enforce temporal progression in multi-principle scenes via a hierarchical stage-level objective.

blocks.en: RL-based Video Generation Prior work adapts preference learning to video along several axes. VideoDPO [ 26 ] extends DPO to text-to-video diffusion with an omni-preference objective balancing visual quality and text relevance. Flow-DPO [ 24 ] aligns flow-matching video generators using a multi-dimensional reward, improving motion smoothness and prompt adherence over SFT and alternative RLHF variants. More fine-grained supervision has also been explored via DenseDPO [ 44 ] , which targets temporal locality by densifying video preferences across time. Complementary directions include GRPO variants tailored to video control, such as DanceGRPO [ 46 ] for learning temporally coherent policies. Additionally, methods such as [ 42 , 7 ] provide global supervision over state properties. Unlike these methods, HiPhy is the first to handle multi-principle physical scenes by integrating a hierarchical objective that targets per-principle optimization in its training.

blocks.en: 4 Method
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en: Given a user prompt q q describing n n concurrent physical principles and a frozen text-to-video model 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , HiPhy learns a policy π θ \pi_{\theta} such that the video v = 𝒢 ⁡ ( p ) v=\mathcal{G}(p) generated from p ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ q ) p\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q) depicts all n n principles with the correct temporal progression of their sub-stages. Two insights shape this design: (i) Modern video models already possess strong visual priors over individual physical phenomena but lack explicit temporal structure for how a physical event should unfold; surfacing this structure at the prompt level is therefore more sample-efficient than retraining the backbone, (ii) Generating complex physical scenes demands compositional reasoning; a video may generate one physical principle faithfully yet fail to compose multiple principles together. We train a reasoning policy π θ \pi_{\theta} via GRPO [ 32 ] using a hierarchical compositional objective. By explicitly isolating each concurrent physical principle and enforcing the temporal progression of its individual sub-stages, our policy guarantees the structural integrity of compound scenes.

blocks.en: We construct a 50K-prompt training dataset and introduce MultiPhyBench, a 1000-prompt evaluation suite in which each prompt describes up to three simultaneous physical events. To generate these, we extract single-principle processes and their domains from VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and WISA-80k [ 39 ] , sample combinations of 1–3 events, and use an LLM [ 47 ] to filter out implausible co-occurrences. For each valid combination, we generate a unified video prompt and a chronologically ordered hierarchical tree for each constituent principle (Fig. 2 ). These hierarchical annotations serve as pseudo-labels for our local reward (Sec. 4.2 ). Full curation details are provided in the SM A .

We introduce HiPhy , a hierarchical physical alignment framework that scores the temporal progression of each physical principle in a fine-grained fashion (see Fig. 3 for an overview).
Consider an input prompt p p describing n n physical principles { p ( i ) } i = 1 n \{p^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{n} . During data curation, each physical principle p ( i ) p^{(i)} is paired with an ordered tree 𝒯 ∗ ( i ) \mathcal{T}^{*(i)} of depth D ( i ) D^{(i)} in which each node represents a stage within that physical principle. For “an apple falls into water and submerges,” the outer level nodes are falling → \rightarrow splash on contact → \rightarrow submerging . The stage splash on contact then further expands into impact → \rightarrow crown formation (Fig. 2 ). Nodes in each level are temporally ordered, meaning that the completion of one node depends on the completion of the nodes before it. During training, we generate a video, v ^ \hat{v} , using a backbone video diffusion model, 𝒢 \mathcal{G} noted as v ^ = 𝒢 ⁡ ( p ) \hat{v}=\mathcal{G}(p) . To evaluate how well the generated video, v ^ \hat{v} , depicts each physical principle { p ( i ) } i = 1 n \{p^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{n} , we extract a similar hierarchical structure as 𝒯 ∗ ( i ) \mathcal{T}^{*(i)} from v ^ \hat{v} for each physical principle p ( i ) p^{(i)} . This procedure is done in the same way as detailed in SM Sec. A . Formally, given a VLM extractor, ℛ \mathcal{R} , we derive an observed tree, 𝒯 ^ ( i ) = ℛ ⁡ ( v ^ , p ( i ) ) \hat{\mathcal{T}}^{(i)}=\mathcal{R}(\hat{v},p^{(i)}) , that decomposes the observed stages in the generated video into a hierarchically ordered tree.

blocks.en: Global Video Reward. The local reward captures fine-grained temporal progression within each process but does not guarantee that the video is semantically faithful to the prompt, visually coherent, or consistent with broader physical commonsense. We introduce a global reward term R global R_{\text{global}} with three complementary terms. First, HPSv2 [ 43 ] captures visual quality and aesthetic alignment, averaged over T T uniformly sampled frames to obtain R HPS R_{\text{HPS}} . Second, a physics VLM judge 𝒥 \mathcal{J} (VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] ) rates physical commonsense R PC R_{\text{PC}} , assessing whether the primary action follows real-world physical rules, and semantic alignment R SA R_{\text{SA}} , measuring whether events described in q q actually appear in v ^ \hat{v} . All three terms are linearly normalized to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] and combined into a single scalar: R global ​ ( v ^ , q ) = w h ​ R ~ HPS + w p ​ R ~ PC + w s ​ R ~ SA , R_{\text{global}}(\hat{v},q)=w_{h}\tilde{R}_{\text{HPS}}+w_{p}\tilde{R}_{\text{PC}}+w_{s}\tilde{R}_{\text{SA}}, (6) Because all three terms characterize whole-video quality, we treat R global R_{\text{global}} as a single reward stream. Together, R PC R_{\text{PC}} guards against gross physical implausibility that local rewards may overlook, R SA R_{\text{SA}} anchors generation to prompt semantics, and R HPS R_{\text{HPS}} favors visually coherent outputs.

To prevent high-variance streams from dominating the GRPO [ 32 ] gradient, we independently normalize each stream within the group [ 28 ] : A hier ( i , j ) = R hier ( i , j ) − μ i σ i + ϵ , A global ( j ) = R global ( j ) − μ g σ g + ϵ , \displaystyle A_{\text{hier}}^{(i,j)}=\frac{R_{\text{hier}}^{(i,j)}-\mu_{i}}{\sigma_{i}+\epsilon},\quad A_{\text{global}}^{(j)}=\frac{R_{\text{global}}^{(j)}-\mu_{g}}{\sigma_{g}+\epsilon}, (7) where μ \mu and σ \sigma denote the per-stream mean and standard deviation across the G G rollouts. Summing these unit-variance local streams directly would scale the overall variance by 𝒪 ⁡ ( n ) \mathcal{O}(n) , disproportionately skewing the gradient for prompts with more principles. To maintain consistent variance regardless of n n , we rescale the local sum by 1 / n 1/\sqrt{n} : A sum ( j ) = A global ( j ) + 1 n ​ ∑ i = 1 n A hier ( i , j ) . A_{\text{sum}}^{(j)}=A_{\text{global}}^{(j)}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{\text{hier}}^{(i,j)}. blocks.en: 5.2 Qualitative Comparisons
blocks.zh: 5.2 定性比较

blocks.en: Figure 4 illustrates the diverse physical principles our method handles compared to the Wan [ 38 ] backbone. Scenes span rigid-body dynamics ( bouncing ball, sliced apple, catching a baseball ), fluid-rigid interactions ( leaf falling into a puddle ), athletic motion ( somersault, skateboarding ), and concurrent multi-principle events ( smoke beside dripping honey , squeezing toothpaste ). In these scenarios, Wan frequently fails: balls bounce implausibly or multiply randomly, leaves disappear into water rather than floating, and athletic motions collapse. Conversely, our method generates each process with accurate temporal progression.
blocks.zh: 图4显示了我们的方法处理与Wan[38]骨干相比的各种物理原理。 镜头横跨刚性身体动力学(弹球、被切成苹果、接住棒球)、流体-刚性相互作用(叶子倒入水坑)、运动运动(滑板和滑板)以及同时发生的多原则事件(滴出蜂蜜旁边的烟雾、挤牙膏)。 在这些假想中,Wan经常失败:球弹出不合理或随机相乘,叶子会消失在水中而不是漂浮,运动运动会倒塌. 相反,我们的方法产生每个过程 精确的时间进展。

blocks.en: Figure 5 compares our method against Wan and three physics-aware baselines: inference-time optimization (Predict-and-Perturb [ 16 ] ), iterative LLM refinement (PhyT2V [ 45 ] ), and finetuning (WISA [ 39 ] ). The results reveal consistent baseline failure modes that compound as the physical event count increases. On two-principle prompts like “ book sliding while a ball falls ”, Fig. 5 , a , baselines struggle with coherent interaction: Wan and PnP omit the sliding book , PhyT2V hallucinates extra objects, and WISA produces static scenes. Similarly, in Fig. 5 , b , gradual integration is often skipped. This performance gap widens on three-principle prompts (bottom). Baselines routinely drop key elements, such as the simmering sauce or rain in Fig. 5 , c , or the boiling water and whisking action in Fig. 5 , d . In contrast, our method coherently generates all constituent processes without degrading overall video quality, which we attribute to optimizing each process as a separate local reward stream during training.
blocks.zh: 图5比较了我们的方法与Wan和三个具有物理意识的基线:推论时间优化(Predict-and-Perturb [16]),迭代LLM改进(PhyT2V [45])和微调(WISA [39])。 结果显示,随着物理事件数的增加,基准故障模式是一致的。 在两个原则的提示上, Wan和PnP省略了"滑行本",PhyT2V产生了额外的物体幻觉,而WISA产生了静态场景. 同样,在图5b中,逐步的融合往往被忽略。 这一业绩差距在三个原则的提示(下方)上有所扩大。 基线通常会减少关键要素,如图5、c中的浸出酱汁或雨水,或图5中的沸水和刮发动作等。 相比之下,我们的方法在不降低整体视频质量的情况下,连贯地生成所有组成过程,我们将此归因于优化每个过程,将其作为培训期间单独的当地奖励流。

blocks.en: 5.3 Quantitative Experiments
blocks.zh: 5.3 定量实验

blocks.en: Table 1: Comprehensive evaluation across VideoPhy2, PhyWorldBench, Multi-concept, and VBench, and ablation experiments over different reward terms
blocks.zh: 表1:全VideoPhy2、PhyWorld的综合评价 座椅、多概念和V Bench, 以及不同奖励条件的消化实验

blocks.en:
We evaluate our method across multiple physical benchmarks such as Videophy2 and PhyWorldBench [ 4 , 10 ] . We assess physical commonsense (PC) and semantic alignment (SA) using Gemini 3 Flash [ 36 ] , which supports higher frame rates. Additionally, we report a “PC & SA” metric that measures the fraction of videos that are simultaneously physically grounded and semantically aligned. To assess robustness beyond physics-specific benchmarks, we also compare against baselines on VBench [ 15 ] , summarizing its orthogonal dimensions into two axes: Dynamics (subject and background consistency, motion smoothness, dynamic degree) and Appearance (imaging and aesthetic quality). Table 1 reports results across two single-principle benchmarks (VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and PhyWorldBench [ 10 ] ) and our curated multi-principle benchmark of 1K prompts containing concurrent physical principles. HiPhy achieves the strongest performance on all physics benchmarks. Our method significantly outperforms the best baselines on VideoPhy2 (+10% physical, +16% alignment) and PhyWorldBench ( ≈ \approx +30% physical, +45% semantic), demonstrating the strength of our hierarchical reward. While generating concurrent physical events remains challenging across all methods, our per-principle hierarchical optimization preserves distinct learning signals, maintaining the largest margin on the multi-principle benchmark.
Finally, VBench [ 15 ] evaluations confirm that physics-aware training preserves general video quality. Both Dynamics and Appearance match or exceed the Wan2.1 baseline, as our global reward terms effectively anchor overall coherence.

This consistency validates our per-process reward design, which ensures each physical principle receives a distinct learning signal.

blocks.en: 5.5 Computational Efficiency.
blocks.zh: 5.5 计算效率。

blocks.en: We compare the inference time of our method against prior physics-grounded video generation baselines on a single H200 GPU. PhyT2V [ 45 ] relies on iterative VLM-based prompt refinement and re-generation, incurring substantial overhead on top of the base video model. PnP [ 16 ] incurs extra computation for its extra optimization steps during inference. WISA [ 39 ] introduces moderate cost through fine-tuned LoRA. In contrast, HiPhy runs once before generation and adds only ∼ \sim 2.4 seconds of overhead, making the total inference time effectively identical to the base model while achieving stronger physical grounding.
blocks.zh: 我们比较了我们方法的推论时间 和之前在H200GPU上 以物理为基础的视频生成基线 PhyT2V [45] 依靠基于VLM的迭代即时改进和再生,在基站视频模型上引起大量间接费用. PnP [16] 在推论中需要额外计算其额外的优化步骤. WISA [39]通过微调的LORA引入了中度成本. 相形之下,HiPhy在生成前运行了一次,只增加了 \\ sim 2.4 秒的俯冲,使得总推断时间与基模型实际上完全相同,同时实现更强大的物理地平面.

blocks.en: trains with only the local hierarchical rewards summed as a single scalar; and HiPhy (local, normalized) trains the hierarchical reward with normalized streams as in Eq. 8 . The two reward families turn out to be complementary. Training with only the global reward yields strong semantic alignment and visual quality but weaker physical commonsense, since the global reward provides no fine-grained signal about how individual processes unfold over time. Training with only the local reward improves physical commonsense on multi-process scenes but degrades semantic alignment and dynamic degree, as the policy optimizes for stage-level correctness without anchoring to prompt semantics or visual coherence. Combining both with per-stream normalization recovers the best of both, as shown in HiPhy row, further confirming our design choice.

blocks.en: Figure 6 shows that both Wan [ 38 ] and VEO [ 9 ] produce near-static coins on the prompt “a coin dances in a spiral on the table,” despite the motion being well within their generative capacity. Pairing each backbone with HiPhy recovers the spiral trajectory in both cases, supporting our claim that the failure to render physically plausible scenes reflects a representational gap rather than a deficit of visual capability. HiPhy transfers across any backbone with sufficient underlying physical priors without retraining.

blocks.en: Figure 7 (A–C) illustrates performance as the number of concurrent principles per prompt increases. While all methods degrade with rising complexity, baselines exhibit a sharp collapse; PnP and PhyT2V lose approximately half their PC scores between 1- and 3-process prompts, with joint PC & SA scores falling below 20. In contrast, HiPhy maintains a joint score of approximately 50, widening the performance gap as complexity grows. We attribute this robustness to our per-process reward stream, which provides distinct learning signals for each event. This prevents the gradient dilution seen in baselines that attempt to collapse multi-process correctness into a single scalar.

blocks.en: 7 Limitations and Broader Impacts
blocks.zh: 7 限制和更广泛的影响

blocks.en: HiPhy uses a frozen backbone T2V model, so its fidelity is upper-bounded by the visual capacity of the underlying generator, similar to other existing work [ 45 , 48 ] . More broadly, physics-aware generation supports applications in education, scientific visualization, and embodied AI, but more plausible video raises the stakes for misinformation and non-consensual content; we build on public backbones and datasets and encourage provenance tools and responsible-release practices.
blocks.zh: HiPhy使用被冷冻的骨干T2V模型,因此其忠诚度被基础生成器的可视能力所上限,类似于其他已存在的工作 [45,48]. 更广泛地说,物理学认知生成支持教育、科学可视化和体现AI的应用,但更可信的视频增加了错误信息和非共识内容的利害关系;我们建立在公共骨干和数据集上,并鼓励出处工具和负责任的释放做法。

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en: We presented a reinforcement learning approach to physics-grounded video generation that decomposes physical correctness into per-principle local rewards over temporal sub-stages and a global reward for semantic and visual coherence. Across VideoPhy2, PhyWorldBench, and our multi-principle benchmark, HiPhy achieves the strongest physical commonsense and semantic alignment, with the largest margins on prompts containing multiple concurrent principles, where prior methods degrade most sharply. These results suggest that explicit temporal decomposition, combined with a learned refinement signal, is an effective approach to closing the gap between video generation and physical realism.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了一种强化的学习方法,用于物理基的视频生成,将物理正确性分解为对时间分级的每个原则的局部奖励,并对语义和视觉一致性给予全球奖励。 横跨VideoPhy2,PhyWorld Bench,以及我们的多原则基准,HiPhy实现最强的物理常识和语义对接,在包含多个并发原理的提示上拥有最大的边际,其中前作方法降解最快. 这些结果表明,明确的时间分解,加上学习到的完善信号,是缩小视频生成与物理现实性差距的有效方法.

blocks.en: Appendix A Multi-Process Dataset Curation
blocks.zh: 附录 A 多程序数据集校正

blocks.en: Existing physical video datasets and benchmarks evaluate physical plausibility along a single process per prompt (e.g., a ball rolling down an incline or water pouring into a glass). However, real-world scenes routinely involve multiple physical processes unfolding simultaneously. To model physical realism in multi-process settings, we construct a dataset in which each prompt describes multiple concurrent physical events. The number of processes per prompt, n n , scales with the video length; for instance, at 81 frames we support up to three simultaneous processes.
blocks.zh: 现有的物理视频数据集和基准沿每个快件的单个过程(如一球向下滚动一英寸或倒入一玻璃的水)评价物理可信度. 然而,现实世界的场景通常涉及同时展开的多个物理过程。 为了在多进程设置中模拟物理现实主义,我们构建了一个数据集,其中每个提示描述多个同时发生的物理事件. 每个即时, n n, 有视频长度的缩放进程的数目; 例如, 我们最多支持三个同步进程, 共81个帧 。

blocks.en:
We collect single-process physical concepts from existing datasets, including VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and WISA-80k [ 39 ] . For each source prompt, we use a large language model to extract the underlying physical process along with its physics domain. For instance, from the prompt “a bowling ball rolls off a table and hits the ground,” we extract the process “ball rolling and falling” with the domain rigid-body
dynamics ; from “steam rises from a boiling pot,” we extract “water boiling” with the domain thermodynamics .
blocks.zh:

我们用域热力学提取出“水沸”。

blocks.en: We sample subsets of 1, 2, or 3 physical concepts per prompt. To capture the true complexity of real-world scenes, we allow combinations of both inter-domain events (e.g., fluid dynamics paired with rigid-body physics) and simultaneous intra-domain events (e.g., multiple concurrent rigid-body interactions). Because not all sampled combinations describe events that can realistically co-occur within a single scene, we employ an LLM to judge whether a given set of processes is physically compatible, discarding combinations marked as implausible.
blocks.zh: 我们抽取了1,2或3个物理概念的子集 为了捕捉到现实世界场景的真实复杂性,我们允许将域间事件(如与刚体物理相配的流体动力学)和同时发生的域内事件(如多个并发的刚体相互作用)结合起来. 因为并非所有被抽样的组合都描述了在单个场景中可以现实地共同实现的事件,所以我们使用LLM来判断某一组进程是否在物理上兼容,抛弃了被标记为不可信的组合.

blocks.en: For each plausible combination, we generate a natural-language video description that coherently integrates all constituent processes within a single scene. In addition, for each physical process, we generate a sequence of chronologically ordered stages that describe the progression of that process over time (e.g., contact → \rightarrow momentum transfer → \rightarrow deceleration for a collision). These stage annotations serve as pseudo-labels references for the local stage-aware reward described in the next section. Figure 2 the structure of the resulting annotations.
blocks.zh: 对于每种可能的组合,我们生成一个自然语言的视频描述,将所有组成过程一致地融合在一个单一的场景中. 此外,对于每个物理过程,我们生成一个按时间顺序排列的阶段序列,以描述该过程随时间推移而演变的情况(例如,接触---正态转动--正态碰撞减速)。 这些阶段说明作为下一节所描述的当地阶段感知奖励的伪标签参考. 图2 由此产生的说明的结构。

blocks.en: To validate that the sub-stages extracted by our pipeline correspond to events that humans actually perceive in the underlying videos, we conducted a small-scale human study on 50 randomly sampled videos spanning six physics domains. Each video was rated by 5 annotators on a 1–5 Likert scale along two axes: how clearly each sub-stage was depicted and whether the sub-stages occurred in the listed chronological order. Table 4 reports the results. The mean stage-quality rating of 4.21/5 and ordering rating of 4.42/5 indicate that our extracted decompositions are faithful to the videos at both the level of individual sub-stages and their temporal arrangement. Scores are consistent across domains, with optics events scoring lowest (3.88), reflecting the difficulty of extracting discrete temporal stages from scenes dominated by events such as reflection and scattering. Furthermore, We conduct a human evaluation survey on whether extracted stages are physically valid. Each of the 50 videos was rated by all 5 raters, giving 250 individual ratings, and the resulting estimates are precise with mean pairwise percent agreement of 0.853 0.853 , with inter-rater agreement of 0.861 0.861 using Gwet’s AC2.

blocks.en: Each stream is standardized against its own mean and standard deviation over the group, so every principle contributes comparably to the advantage. Without it, a stream that varies more widely dominates and the policy maximizes that one term while ignoring the rest, degrading alignment and multi-process scenes (second row). The 1 n \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} rescaling addresses a different problem. Summing more terms inflates the variance of the advantage, so a three-principle sample pushes the gradient harder than a one-principle sample; the rescaling holds this variance constant. It also preserves the balance between the two reward families, since the advantage combines one global stream with a sum of n local ones. Without the factor the local sum overwhelms the global term and the policy loses the signal anchoring generation to prompt semantics and visual coherence, visible as the SA drop in the third row. At N = 1 N=1 the factor is inactive and per-stream normalization has little to balance, with only one local stream alongside the global one; the differences emerge as principles co-occur.

blocks.en: To complement the automatic evaluations, we analyze survey results for videos containing multiple concurrent physical principles. We report the average ratings from 50 participants who evaluated the depiction of each physical event; a representative question from this study is shown in Fig. 8 .
